advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Guard _resolve_system against routing a {{shared_prefix}}-bearing template (e.g. PASS_VERIFIER) through the SHARED_STANCE_PREAMBLE-prepending else-branch, which would double the preamble.
evidence: passes.py:281-283: `if prompt_id == PASS_FINDER:\n        return prompts.shared_plan_prefix(plan) + body\n    return prompts.SHARED_STANCE_PREAMBLE + body`
The verifier templates render {{shared_prefix}} = shared_plan_prefix(plan), which itself begins with SHARED_STANCE_PREAMBLE (prompts.py:373-382), so the else-branch prepend would duplicate it.
Ticket 9374 rationale: PASS_VERIFIER removed from the hygiene loop because keeping it 'would render a doubled preamble' — an acknowledged latent trap, not code-guarded.
advisory.finding: _resolve_system(PASS_VERIFIER, ...) would emit a DOUBLED reviewing-stance preamble: the else-branch prepends SHARED_STANCE_PREAMBLE while the verifier template also embeds it via its {{shared_prefix}} var. It is safe today only because no live caller routes the verifier prompt through _resolve_system, but the branch offers no guard/assertion against that future misuse.
scenarios: A future maintainer re-introduces a bespoke Pass-2 verifier call through _resolve_system(PASS_VERIFIER, ...) and silently ships a prompt with the stance preamble twice.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add an explicit guard (e.g. `assert prompt_id != PASS_VERIFIER` or a branch that recognizes shared_prefix-embedding templates) so the doubled-preamble misuse fails loudly rather than silently.
